body:
On the Theory and Practice of Pretending to be Better Than You Are


Being an Essay on the Various Stratagems That May Make One Appear Skilled


Introduction

It is generally a widely-accepted fact that when it comes to most things in life, some people are good at them and some people are bad at them. Minecraft PvP is no exception. Being bad at Minecraft PvP is usually not terribly fun or glamorous, and it often takes many hours of practice to get better, something that many people do not have the time or the patience for. Fortunately, there is another way for people who want to “get good” fast, or at least appear to be so. With a significantly smaller time investment, it is quite easy to misrepresent one’s skill level to other people by utilizing several simple strategies that can be learned in less than an hour. At last, there is a solution for people who want to “be “better at Minecraft PvP without all that tedious effort. That solution, of course, is the subject of this essay and much of my research for the past several months. If you follow my methods, I guarantee you that you will appear to be much better at PvP to people who do not ever actually get a chance to fight you.


The Importance of K/D

Perhaps the best way to get a quick measure of someone’s PvP skill is to check their K/D, which luckily for us is easy to access for anyone right on this website. In order to maintain a high K/D, preferably above 1.0, the most important thing is to start early. If you’ve got 30,000 kills and 40,000 deaths, it’s probably already too late for you unless you like grinding a lot. If you happen to be that person, you’ve got several options. The best one is to purchase a new Minecraft account, change the name of your main account, wait 37 days, change the name of your new account to that of your former main account, and then start playing with that account with a clean slate. Another option is to try and convince some of the senior staff to wipe all of your stats. The final option, and by far the most extreme, is to hack into the Avicus server and whatnot and erase your stats, which I will not go further into detail about because I’m relatively certain it’s slightly against the law. Anyhow, a high K/D will make you appear to be good at PvP upon a cursory inspection of your profile page online, but even if they don’t happen to do that merely getting lots of kills and dying very little on the server will make you appear pretty good as well.


Strategies for getting kills:

Knocking people out of the world

Scientifically, the easiest way to kill someone is to knock them out of the world. Knocking someone out of the world is basically an instakill, and it’s very efficient as well, being probably the absolute quickest way to kill someone. It’s also quite good because in many cases whoever you knocked out probably didn’t get very many hits off on you, making it more difficult to be killed by his friends or that guy standing out there with the bow. The best strategy for knocking people out of the world is to take advantage of poor positioning on your target’s part and knock them out real quick while you stay safely on the inside of whatever landmass you may be standing on. The best time to knock people out of the world is when they are running and jumping (and often making a mess placing blocks all around) through your base and trying to get to your monument or wool, because usually they will have poor positioning, won’t be fighting back,and if you hit them mid-jump they’ll be knocked back pretty damn far.


Bowing

“Bowing” is technically not the correct word but for the purposes of this essay it is clearest word to use. Basically, using the bow a lot will net you plenty of kills with little to no risk. The easiest bow strategy is to knock people on thin skybridges off where they will either die of fall damage or from falling out of the world (or not at all if they have water or whatever). Knocking people off skybridges is a good strategy for the whole game, but the best time to do so is at the beginning of the round when many of them are poorly developed or still being built. Another good bow strategy is to stand on top of an incline and shoot people who are trying to climb up it, if you “bow-spam” and fire lots of arrows they’ll die eventually without ever getting up the incline, however please note that some people look down on so-called “bow-spammers”. Outside of these two situations, the best thing to do with the bow is to stand back in your base and “snipe” people, thus exposing yourself to minimal risk while netting kills here and there.


“Kill-securing/Last-hitting/Teaming”

It is perhaps historically true that having more of things gives you an advantage, with several notable exceptions such as cancer. In any case, one of the best ways to kill a person is to attack with two people. To take advantage of this fact, try to stick together with your teammates or if you see one struggling in a brutal 1v1, run in and kindly offer your aid. Once you’ve got two people whacking away at someone, they should go down pretty quick no matter how bad you are at PvP, and roughly half the time you’ll get the credit for the kill since you’ll get the coveted “last-hit”, which is good for farming gold credits. If you happen to go with the first option, which is following a teammate around, make sure you let your teammate go in and initiate fights because that’ll mean they’ll take on most of the risk/damage and there’s even a chance they’ll die and you can come in and sweep up for an easy kill.


Getting Good Gear (GG...G)

Exploiting anything that can give you an advantage is important for anyone bad at PvP looking to get kills, and luckily there’s plenty of stuff on maps to help you. The most basic example, of course, is getting iron armor, since there’s always many people who don’t bother with it. However, some maps have opportunities for getting even better gear, such as diamonds for diamond armor and swords, or bows enchanted with Punch/Flame/Power. The only thing I can recommend when it comes to getting diamonds is to learn where they are and rush for them, and as for the good bows they are usually hidden in chests around the maps so just look around a map the first time you play it and see if you can find any of them.


Strategies for not dying


“Deathzones”

Probably the best way to avoid dying is to avoid places where dying happens often. Luckily, I’ve figured out where those places are, and they happen to be skybridges and the enemy base. Basically, the best way to not die is to stay on defense, outside of heavily contested areas (or dangerously thin skybridges), because there’s fewer enemies and you’ve always got places full of teammates to run to if you are dying.


Staying away from good people

If you ever get just completely destroyed by a person (which likely occurs often to you if you are reading this), be sure to take note of their name and stay away from them in the future and be content with just bowing them from afar unless you’ve got some kind’ve big advantage over them.


Staying away from people with better gear

If you’ve only got leather armor, it’s pretty damn hard to kill someone in iron armor or (god forbid) diamond armor, so if you see someone who’s got better gear than you the best option is to run far away. The only exception is if you have a golden opportunity to knock them out of the world, in which case I say take it because there’s nothing like imagining the look on some full diamond’s face when you kill them in 2 hits when you’ve got only leather since you managed to hit them out. Another thing to note is that it’s probably a good idea to stay away from people who have the same armor as you (with the exception of the armor that everyone spawns with) because that means you’ll be fighting on equal footing, something you definitely do not want to be doing.


Explaining away your deaths

Another important thing to do if you are trying to look good is to have excuses for your deaths, so that people are misdirected from the actual reason of your death, which is likely lack of skill. Fortunately, there are plenty of excuses that I’ve come up with and that I’ve seen people like me use in the past, so there’s good variety and you can keep each excuse nice and fresh. These excuses are mainly intended for use in voice chats, however if you feel inclined you may type them in the server chat as well (although I do not recommend it unless someone is trying to accuse you of being bad).


Ping

The effect of having low ping or high ping on gameplay is little understood, however what is known is that having unusually high or low ping can be paradoxically both good and bad. The good thing is that ping goes both ways, so you can blame your own ping or your opponents ping. The best times to use this particular excuse is when you or your opponent has unusually high or low ping, which can be seen on the tablist. Generally, low ping is when the bar is completely full (and as a result it’s very difficult to tell if anyone actually has low ping since anything from 1-100 ping is a full bar) and high ping is when the bar is anything but completely fall.

Here are several examples of what you can say after you die to blame the death on ping:

“holy shit the server must be hosted on that dude’s computer”

“jesus christ this is what we get for fighting teams from botswana”

“good god in heaven my ping is in the stratosphere today, fuck comcast”

“literally cannot hit that dude, he’s teleporting around like a fucking enderman”

You can always accuse your opponent of being a “pinger”, which seems to be an ill-defined general insult, or if your opponents ping suddenly gets very high, accuse them of using the fabled “lagswitch”, which may or may not exist.


Frames

Another good thing to blame deaths on is a low framerate. Generally, not having a good framerate can impede one’s ability to play the game, and it can be caused by any number of things. The good thing about framerate is that other players cannot see your framerate, as opposed to ping, so blaming deaths on framerate is a lot easier because you don’t have to hope that you or your opponent have usually high or low ping. If anyone asks why your framerate is so low, the best thing to do is to just go off on some rant about how your computer fucking sucks and how you don’t have enough goddamn money to get anything better or talk about how you have dozens of tabs open and that you should probably close some of them.


Some examples of what you can say:

“holy shit my frames dropped like an anchor when i fought that dude, i should probably close some of these internet explorer windows”

“jesus christ why the hell does my shitty-ass graphics card only work when i’m NOT fighting people”

“good god in heaven if my framerate drops below 30 one more time i am going to personally murder notch”

“god DAMMIT i got fucking optifine and still this BULLSHIT frames shit happens”


Hacks

Accusing your opponent of hacking after dying is probably hands down one of the best ways to explain away your death. First off, it subtly suggests that the only way you can be beat is with hacks, although it’s unlikely anyone will pick up on this. The best part is how difficult it is to prove someone is not hacking beyond a doubt, since even if they get screenshared and whatnot it’s child’s play to delete a few folders beforehand. The only drawback is that this only really works on players who are pretty good at the game, since otherwise no one would believe they’re hacking, but eventually some people may start agreeing with you that the person is hacking if they are just that good. There are quite a few hacks out there, and it’s usually best practice to name one or two when you make an accusation, so here’s a list of a few select ones:


X-ray: This one, pretty obviously, lets you see through blocks. Best used when someone finds you when you are tunnelling.

Tracers: Lets you find players easily by like drawing lines to them or something I dunno. The only important part is that it makes finding players far easier, so use it if you get caught sneaking around or tunnelling.

Reach: Lets you hit people from further away, good to use if you get combo’ed pretty hard.

Autoclicker: The name says it all, good for when someone is constantly clicking, building super fast, or hitting super fast

Fly: Again, very self-explanatory. Best to use if you were in a situation where you got very close to knocking someone off but they “flew” back up and killed you.

Fastbow: Turns your bow into a machinegun. Very visible, so you should probably only blame deaths that actually happen because of fastbow on it.

Killaura: Basically just hits anyone who comes within a certain distance, pretty good all around but especially good if someone takes a 2v1 and lives.

Aimbot: Like locks onto players so that they can be hit easily or something, I don’t really know, but this is another all around good one.

Anti-Knockback: This is another good one to use if you get very close to knocking someone off and they kill you, it basically just reduces knockback.

That’s about as many I remember, there’s certainly more but they are pretty obscure and don’t really matter a whole lot for the purposes of this essay.


Things to say:

“holy shit this dude takes NO goddamn knockback if he doesn’t have antikb i will literally eat a bag of dicks”

“jesus christ that dude hit me from literally across the whole fucking map”

“good god in heaven the only way that dude can possibly have cps that high legit is if he had fucking epilepsy”


Windows update

Almost everyone has been there: everything is going great, mining the thing or whatever and then suddenly ba-bam! Windows interrupts your day to say it wants to update or just jumps straight to the update. I don’t know if Macs (gross) do the same thing, but before you try to blame anything on OSX updates make sure you do the research first. Anyways, this one is pretty good because a lot of people can relate and it feels like it happens all the damn time, but use this excuse sparingly because people will get suspicious if you have more than one update per day or week or even perhaps month.


What to say:

“the next time fucking windows update decides to dick me over again like this i am going to move to montana and start sending bombs in the mail to microsoft holy fuck”


Pets
 Do you have a cat and/or dog? If you don’t, you do now, and guess what their favorite activity is? That’s right, crawling all over your face/keyboard whenever you are trying to play Minecraft. This one’s truly a classic, but make sure you do a little research about what breed your fake dog/cat is if you don’t have one and make sure to have some cute little stories prepared if people ask. Anyone who doesn’t have a dog or cat but wants to take the whole scam a bit further can prepare some meowing/barking on their phone and play it into their mic, or even practice and get good at doing meowing/barking themselves. The sky's the limit with this one, and I suppose if you are really willing to take it to the logical extreme you can go out and actually get a dog/cat but please note it’s a lot of goddamn work.


What to say:

“holy shit cat get off my keyboard or i swear to god i am not going to feed you for the next week”

“jesus christ if i knew this dog would be so much fucking trouble i would’ve never taken it from that bum on the side of the road”
